name: @material-tax-reporting/slip-parser
description: Local-only Canadian tax slip and receipt parsing contracts with mandatory manual confirmation.
//: The '.' entry is conditional because a bare '.ts' entry point is a trap for
Node, and this package was carrying one.
Bundlers take 'default' and read the TypeScript source directly. Node takes
'node' and reads ./dist/index.js, because Node cannot load a '.ts' file: it
strips types only when asked until 22.18.0, and the toolchain this repository
pins is older than that (22.14.0 in the root manifest and the release
workflow, 22.13.0 in the documentation-site workflow). Before this entry
existed, the first file Node executed directly that imported this package by
name would have died on that import with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION naming
src/index.ts. A sibling package in this repository shipped exactly that entry
and broke two builds with it.
Nothing imports this package yet, so this is prevention rather than a repair:
no workspace declares it as a dependency and no source file imports it. That
also means ./dist is not built by anything today. 'npm run build' in this
package writes it, and THE FIRST CONSUMER MUST RUN THAT BUILD FROM ITS OWN
'prebuild' IN THE SAME CHANGE THAT ADDS THE IMPORT — the way the desktop
workspace already does for the surface kernel. Wiring a hook here instead
would be a build step no workspace runs. A consumer that reaches the 'node'
condition without building gets ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND naming dist/index.js,
which says what to do; the failure it replaces did not.
./dist is generated and git-ignored, so the compiled entry is never a tracked
file. scripts/stage-offline-ocr-assets.mjs is unaffected by all of this: the
Windows packaging script spawns it by file path rather than by package name,
so it never consults this map, and it imports only node: builtins.
